A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ScaleBiO and contain readable main text, algorithms, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Retained, relocated, and newly added material can be reliably distinguished.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2 experiments, learned data weights for larger models, and MT-Bench fine-tuning and weight-transfer results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds comparative instruction-following and mathematical-reasoning results, including competition-math evaluations in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: The softmax source weights, penalty-based minimax objective, auxiliary model, and single-loop randomized block updates remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 gains explanatory comments and an iteration-index typo correction, without introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds dedicated mathematical-reasoning training using a ten-source mixture, evaluation on GSM8K and MATH, and AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and AIMO 2025 experiments using DeepSeek-R1-generated reasoning data. The earlier GPT-2 scenarios and 18-source instruction-following coverage remain.

E2.justification: The MT-Bench comparison expands from uniform sampling to LESS, RHO-LOSS, and attempted SOBA comparisons reported as out of memory in v2 Table 2. LESS and RHO-LOSS also participate in the new mathematical-reasoning comparisons; their earlier citations alone did not constitute evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported model learning-rate setting changes from a fixed 10^-5 to a search over eight values. New protocols include Qwen and Gemma backbones, 20K-sample mathematical fine-tuning, validation/tuning splits, and 4K-sample DeepSeek distillation evaluated with pass@1 and cons@64. These do not establish that retained MT-Bench results were rerun.

E4.justification: The source-weight analysis expands to Qwen and Gemma and adds mathematical-reasoning weight profiles in v2 Tables 7–8, examining preferences across model families and tasks. The Yi-34B weight trajectory in v1 Figure 4 is removed. The GPT-2 demonstrations and 8B-to-70B transfer analysis remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-training-run summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new cons@64 evaluation is a performance metric, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial MT-Bench and mathematical-reasoning results. For example, Table 5 reports Qwen-2.5-32B accuracies of 87.1/59.8 on GSM8K/MATH versus uniform sampling's 78.1/54.0. The earlier Llama-3-8B MT-Bench scores of 6.11 versus 7.12 and 70B transfer scores of 7.85 versus 8.05 remain unchanged. v1's category-level MT-Bench results are removed.

T1.justification: v2 removes the explicit implicit-function derivation in v1 Equation 3 and makes sampling independence explicit in Appendix D. The main theorem, convergence rate, and proof argument remain intact. Appendix C also rewrites Lemma 6's threshold using undefined symbols, introducing a localized formal-reporting defect rather than a new guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements expand from demonstrating filtering and instruction-tuning benefits to claiming superiority over named strong baselines in instruction following and mathematical reasoning. The headline scalability claim changes from 34B parameters on eight A40 GPUs to approximately 30B on eight H100 GPUs. The central first-order optimization and conditional convergence claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes broadly shared preferred sources and concentration of over 80% of weight in three sources. v2's Discussion instead emphasizes model-family-dependent preferences, conjecturally linked to pretraining distributions, and argues against universal optimal mixtures for small datasets. Appendix A.2 also attributes the reduced cons@64 advantage to limited data diversity. The existing pretraining and safety limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds baseline optimizer and LoRA settings, reference-model details, tuning information, FSDP, approximately 6K GPU hours, and mathematical-data access and licensing information. Hardware reporting changes to H100, replacing v1's A100 implementation statement and A40 abstract claim. Conversely, v1's explicit ScaleBiO code link disappears, and the new uniform-sampling calculation incorrectly states 10,000/18 as approximately 5556.

R1.justification: The related-work framework remains largely intact, but Table 1 adds SAMA and (FG)2U, and the stated previous scalability ceiling changes from over 1B to over 3B parameters. The introduction adds data-quality, fairness, and robustness literature, with further references supporting the new experiments.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, and application narrative receive substantial rewriting. Large-scale experiments are reorganized by task, implementation details move into Appendix B.2, and a dedicated Discussion section replaces parts of the earlier interpretation. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. v2 introduces several comparison and dataset tables, expands and relocates the source-weight table to Appendix A.1, and separates retained MT-Bench results across displays. Figures 1–3 are retained and resized, while v1 Figure 4 and its category-level MT-Bench table are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited downstream evidence, which mainly compared against uniform sampling on MT-Bench. Stronger comparators, multiple model families, and dedicated mathematical-reasoning evaluations make the effectiveness claim much better supported; expanded implementation details and model-dependent interpretation also help. These gains outweigh the removed code link and category breakdown and localized reporting errors. Uncertainty estimates remain absent, and Table 9 includes ties despite broad outperformance wording.
